Routing notes:
- Do not default to option C. It was rejected on 9 of 10 observed tickets; rejection message: “option C is not valid for this request.”
- The only confirmed valid/useful case for C: REQ-2408, a small shipment from the north region, with “Second attempt, the first form bounced,” routed to C (regional …) successfully.
- No reliable rule yet distinguishes A (standard queue) from B (priority desk), or determines when C is valid.
- Treat request type, region, size, sender/team, and message wording as potentially relevant, but do not infer a routing rule from the current evidence alone.
- When C is not explicitly supported/fully described in the options, prefer evaluating A or B rather than guessing C.

Routing notes:
- Do not default to B: rejected in all 3 new attempts (REQ-2413–2415), including large east claims/invoices. B is currently unsupported.
- A has mixed but informative results: accepted REQ-2410 (small east claim), REQ-2418 (small south claim), and REQ-2419 (small south shipment); rejected REQ-2411, 2412, 2416 (large requests) and REQ-2417 (small east shipment).
- A appears more promising for some small requests, but size alone is not a reliable rule: a small east shipment with “Same as the ones I sent last month” was rejected, while similarly worded/sized requests elsewhere succeeded.
- Large requests observed so far all rejected under A or B (north invoice/shipment; east claim/invoice; south shipment). This may indicate C, but no new C success confirms that inference.
- Prior confirmed C success remains REQ-2408: small north shipment, “Second attempt, the first form bounced,” with regional-office C.
- Wording is not decisive: “Second attempt…” succeeded with C previously but A succeeded for a small south shipment with the same wording; “No rush…” and “regional office” examples were rejected under A/B.
- Treat request type, region, size, sender/team, wording, and option completeness as potentially relevant, without inferring a deterministic rule.
- When C is explicitly supported and the request resembles the known regional-office case—especially when A/B appear unsupported—evaluate C; otherwise prefer A over B only when evidence supports it, and avoid guessing from truncated option text.

Routing notes:
- Do not default to B: rejected in all three recent attempts (REQ-2413–2415); B remains unsupported.
- C is also currently unsupported in the latest batch: rejected on REQ-2420 and REQ-2422–2429, including north/east/south, small/large, and multiple request types. Do not infer C from region, size, wording, or incomplete option text.
- The prior confirmed C success is still REQ-2408: small north shipment, “Second attempt, the first form bounced,” with regional-office C. Treat it as an isolated confirmed case, not a general rule.
- A has mixed results: accepted REQ-2410, 2418, 2419, and REQ-2421 (small east refund); rejected REQ-2411, 2412, 2416, 2417, and REQ-2423 (small east invoice). A is preferable to B/C only where evidence supports it.
- Large requests have so far been rejected under A, B, and now C (including REQ-2422, 2424–2426, 2429). Size alone does not identify the correct option.
- Wording is not decisive: “Second attempt,” “No rush,” and “Same as last month” have produced mixed or rejected outcomes; sender/team, request type, region, size, wording, and option completeness may all matter.
- Avoid guessing from truncated options. Use only confirmed precedents; absent a close match, recognize that current evidence does not establish a reliable deterministic routing rule.

Routing notes:
- Do not default to B: rejected in all recent attempts (REQ-2413–2415); still unsupported.
- C remains unsupported in the latest batch: rejected on REQ-2420 and REQ-2422–2429. Do not infer C from region, size, wording, request type, or incomplete option text. Prior confirmed C success remains isolated to REQ-2408 (small north shipment, regional-office wording).
- A is mixed: accepted REQ-2410, 2418, 2419, 2421 (small east refund), and 2433 (small south claim); rejected REQ-2411, 2412, 2416, 2417, 2423, 2431, 2434, and 2436. Use A only with a close confirmed precedent.
- D is now confirmed as a real option despite often-truncated option listings: accepted REQ-2432 (large north claim, Finance Desk) and REQ-2437 (large east invoice, Field Sales); rejected REQ-2430 and 2435 (large north/south invoices, “No rush”). D is not generally implied by large size, invoice type, or “No rush.”
- D also failed on REQ-2438 and 2439 (small south invoice/claim, Regional Ops), so neither sender/team nor repeated wording alone determines routing.
- Large requests have mixed outcomes under D and remain rejected under A/B/C in prior evidence. Size alone is not predictive.
- Wording remains non-decisive: “No rush,” “Same as last month,” and scanned-paperwork wording produce mixed results.
- Do not guess from truncated options. Use only close confirmed precedents; current evidence still does not establish a reliable deterministic routing rule.

Routing notes:
- Do not default to B: rejected in all observed attempts (REQ-2413–2415); still unsupported.
- C remains unsupported in recent evidence (REQ-2420, 2422–2429); do not infer it from region, size, wording, request type, or truncated option text. The only confirmed C success remains REQ-2408.
- A is mixed. Accepted REQ-2410, 2418, 2419, 2421, 2433, 2443, and 2448; rejected REQ-2411, 2412, 2416, 2417, 2423, 2431, 2434, 2436, 2440, and 2446. Even similar small east shipments produced opposite outcomes, so use A only with exceptionally close confirmed evidence.
- D is a real option but currently unreliable. Accepted REQ-2432 and 2437; rejected REQ-2430, 2435, 2438, 2439, and all recent D attempts REQ-2441, 2442, 2444, 2445, 2447, and 2449. Large size, invoice/claim type, region, sender/team, and wording do not imply D.
- Large requests remain mixed overall and have repeatedly rejected A/B/C in prior evidence. Size alone is not predictive.
- Wording (“No rush,” regional-office wording, scanned paperwork, urgency) is non-decisive; repeated wording can yield different valid routes.
- Do not guess from truncated option listings. No reliable deterministic routing rule is established. Prefer only a genuinely close confirmed precedent, while recognizing that even matching size, region, type, team, and wording may fail.

Routing notes:
- Do not default to B: rejected in all observed attempts (REQ-2413–2415); still unsupported.
- C remains unsupported in recent evidence (REQ-2420, 2422–2429); do not infer it from region, size, wording, request type, or truncated option text. The only confirmed C success remains REQ-2408.
- A remains mixed. New acceptances: REQ-2450, 2452, 2455, 2458, 2459. New rejections: REQ-2451, 2453, 2454, 2456, 2457. Large claims through the regional office succeeded for east and south, but a similar north claim failed; this does not establish a rule.
- D is a real option but unreliable: accepted REQ-2432 and 2437; rejected REQ-2430, 2435, 2438, 2439, and REQ-2441, 2442, 2444, 2445, 2447, 2449. Size, request type, region, sender/team, and wording do not imply D.
- Large requests remain mixed overall and have repeatedly rejected A/B/C. Size alone is not predictive.
- Wording such as regional-office references, scanned paperwork, urgency, “no rush,” or repeated attempts is non-decisive; identical or similar wording can produce different routes.
- Do not guess from truncated option listings. No reliable deterministic routing rule is established. Prefer only a genuinely close confirmed precedent, while recognizing that even matching size, region, type, team, and wording may fail.
